pass_a_gloss: After the Gentiles’ full number enters, it will be saved, having left lawlessness behind; then the end comes, and punishment for worldly things, as we wait for judgment. The word may also be addressed to the church, daughter of the old synagogue—“God’s gifts are irrevocable”—but her lawlessness left via divine baptism; the Speaker no longer gives her to foes, declaring, “Here I will dwell, I chose her,” and “I am with you always until the age’s end,” when impiety was fixed among those focused on earthly matters.
pass_b_english: It will be saved after the full number of the Gentiles has come in, having abandoned lawlessness; then the consummation will follow, and the punishment of earthly things, as we await the judgment. Indeed, the word might also be spoken to the church, which is the daughter of the ancient synagogue, for “the gifts of God are irrevocable,” yet its lawlessness has departed through divine baptism; she whom the Speaker no longer hands over to the enemies says, “Here I will dwell, for I have chosen her,” and “Behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age,” when even impiety was established among those who mind earthly things.
